title: Jon Gray says impatience about AI returns is 'a little misplaced'
excerpt: Jon Gray said that AI applications will take time to show up, and that Blackstone is invested across the AI ecosystem.
content_html:
Good, potentially very lucrative things will come to the AI investors who wait, if you ask Jon Gray.

Gray, the president and chief operating officer at Blackstone, said that growing concern about the pace of the AI buildout is somewhat overblown.

"I'm not going to discount that there's not going to be misallocations of capital. There are people who are doing things that may not turn out to have high returns. But I think the impatience is a little misplaced. It takes some time for the applications to happen," Gray said on an episode of Blackstone's quarterly market views video that aired on July 30.

July was a turbulent month for AI-linked stocks. Chipmaker stocks were hit by jitters in Asian markets. Investors have become increasingly skeptical about the pace of hyperscalers' tremendous AI spending. Meta and Alphabet shares dropped after they each raised yearly AI spending predictions. Gray said that AI will eventually work its way through many business areas, and described the technology as a "new operating system for the global economy."

Blackstone, the world's largest data center investor, is investing heavily across the AI economy. Gray said that one data center creates a ripple effect of economic activity, since it demands investments in chips and power.

When Gray rattled off the firm's biggest deals from the second quarter, almost all of them touched the AI buildout, from chips to semiconductors to data centers. The company recently bought three hotels in the San Francisco area, the country's AI capital. In June, Blackstone bought the Hyatt Regency for $279 million, or about $340,000 per room, according to a press release from the seller.

Revenue for the firm's private equity portfolio grew 11% in the second quarter, a result Gray said was driven by investments in AI. The growth, he said, has "got a long way to run."

content_html_zh:
如果你问乔恩·格雷（Jon Gray），那些等待的人工智能投资者将会得到好的、可能非常有利可图的东西。

黑石集团总裁兼首席运营官格雷表示，对人工智能建设速度的日益担忧有些言过其实。

“我不会否认不会出现资本错配。 有些人所做的事情可能不会带来高回报。 但我认为这种不耐烦有点不合时宜。 申请需要一些时间，”格雷在 7 月 30 日播出的黑石季度市场观点视频中说道。

对于人工智能相关股票来说，七月是动荡的一个月。 芯片制造商的股票受到亚洲市场动荡的打击。 投资者对超大规模企业巨额人工智能支出的步伐越来越怀疑。 Meta 和 Alphabet 各自提高了年度人工智能支出预测后，股价下跌。 格雷表示，人工智能最终将渗透到许多商业领域，并将该技术描述为“全球经济的新操作系统”。

全球最大的数据中心投资者黑石集团正在人工智能经济领域进行大量投资。 格雷表示，一个数据中心会对经济活动产生连锁反应，因为它需要对芯片和电力进行投资。

当格雷逐一列举该公司第二季度最大的交易时，几乎所有交易都涉及人工智能建设，从芯片到半导体再到数据中心。 该公司最近在美国人工智能之都旧金山地区购买了三家酒店。 根据卖方的新闻稿，黑石集团于 6 月以 2.79 亿美元（即每间客房约 34 万美元）收购了凯悦酒店。

该公司私募股权投资组合的收入在第二季度增长了 11%，格雷表示，这是由人工智能投资推动的。 他说，这种增长“还有很长的路要走”。
